answer: An agent economy can price identity in a scarce staked deposit, like a reef that only lets new growth anchor on established limestone. To accept work from an unfamiliar agent, the market makes it lock funds that peers can slash if it misbehaves, so a thousand fake identities cost a thousand slashed deposits, not one cheap alias. Any real nectar of revenue only reaches an operator once its stake has survived scrutiny, and each new dawn of settlements re-checks the same collateral. A sybil swarm therefore burns real capital, not just time.
